cases.description: When no dynamic scopes have been entered, the internal Deque is empty. Calling getDynamicScope() should return null (Deque.peek() returns null on an empty collection).

cases.expected: non-null Scope instance (the one returned by enterDynamicScope())
cases.description: Enter a dynamic scope once and then call getDynamicScope(). The method should return the same Scope object that was pushed onto the internal Deque.

cases.expected: non-null Scope instance (the most recently entered scope)
cases.description: Enter three dynamic scopes sequentially. getDynamicScope() must return the Scope that was entered last (top of the stack), confirming LIFO ordering.

cases.expected: non-null Scope instance (the scope that was entered before the last one)
cases.description: Enter two dynamic scopes, then exit one. getDynamicScope() should now return the first scope that was entered, proving that exitDynamicScope() correctly removes the top element.

cases.description: Enter a single dynamic scope and then exit it. The internal Deque becomes empty, so a subsequent call to getDynamicScope() must return null, similar to the empty‑stack case but reached via state changes.

cases.expected: same Scope instance on consecutive calls
cases.description: Enter a dynamic scope and call getDynamicScope() multiple times without modifying the stack. Each call should return the identical Scope object, confirming that getDynamicScope() does not alter the Deque.
